description:
At origin/main `a3a9761d1209165e5230625b9347cf6b0ad09b83`, function-head exhaustiveness has two deliberately different policies.

- Functions with a declared `@spec` defer their head check until `FunctionContract` and `EntryDispatch` are available. `contract_has_reachable_fail` evaluates each correlated contract input row through `calculate_dispatch_reachability`.
- Functions without a contract are checked immediately in `define_function`. `check_function_clauses` builds domain-free `SourcePatternRows` and asks `is_inexhaustive`, so `[]` + cons is considered partial over all fz values even when every observed caller supplies a list.
- `case` and `with`-else diagnostics remain domain-free body diagnostics.

This is also the documented language behavior in `.agent/docs/pattern-matching.md` and `guides/pattern-matching.html`. Changing it is a policy change, not merely relocating an existing lint.

## Current reproducer

```fz
fn list_total([]), do: 0
fn list_total([_head | tail]), do: 1 + list_total(tail)

fn main(), do: dbg(list_total([1, 2]))
```

`fz2 interp` exits 0 and prints `2`, but emits one `warning[type/no-matching-clause]`. Adding `@spec list_total([integer]) :: integer` makes the same program print `2` with no warning.

The proposed observed-input signal already exists: `AnalyzeActivation` evaluates every correlated `ActivationInputAlternatives` row through `calculate_dispatch_reachability` and records `EntryReachability` with `fail_reachable` ORed across those rows. Any implementation must consume settled semantic authority and emit at most one source warning per function/root; it must not emit from transient activation evidence that can later refine.

## Current corpus

There are 46 `warning[type/no-matching-clause]` entries across 19 `fixtures2/behavior/*.diagnostics` files. 27 point into demanded runtime-library sources:

- `runtime:Enum.fz`: 23
- `runtime:List.fz`: 2
- `runtime:Range.fz`: 1
- `runtime:Map.fz`: 1

`quicksort.expected.diagnostics` still contains two warnings, for `append/2` and `qsort/1`.

The previous text's claim that `map_list` and `with_index_list` were deleted was a grep error: they are private `fnp` definitions at `enum.fz:277-278` and `319-323`.

## Required decision

Choose and document one policy:

1. Keep the current conservative rule: an uncontracted function is callable over all fz values, so domain-free partiality warns; close this ticket after adding a focused regression that makes the rule explicit.
2. Adopt observed-activation coverage: for demanded uncontracted functions, warn only when a settled reachable activation input row can reach `Dispatch Fail`. Declared-contract coverage remains contract-owned, and nested `case`/`with` checks remain independently domain-free.

If policy 2 is chosen, do not create another pattern walker. Reuse the shared `EntryDispatch` reachability result and define how public/dynamic inputs, guarded heads, undemanded functions, multiple roots, and diagnostic deduplication are handled.

## Checks for policy 2

- The `list_total` reproducer emits no warning.
- A sibling repro with an actually reachable non-list input emits exactly one warning.
- A public/dynamic input remains conservative.
- Declared-contract exhaustiveness tests remain unchanged.
- Guard fallthrough stays conservative.
- quicksort's two warnings and all 46 corpus warnings are re-derived from settled reachability; every golden change is explained, not blanket-blessed.
- Update both agent and user-facing pattern-matching documentation.
title: Decide and implement observed-activation exhaustiveness for uncontracted function heads
